verses.text: Paul, an apostle (sent one) of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
To the saints (holy people) and faithful brothers in Christ who are at Colosse: Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. We pray always for you.
We heard of your faith in Christ Jesus. We heard of the love which you have to all the saints (holy people).
This is because of the hope which is laid up for you in heaven. You heard of this hope before in the word of the truth of the gospel (good news).

The gospel (good news) has come to you, as it is in all the world. It brings forth fruit, as it does also in you. It has done so since the day you heard of it. That day you knew the grace of God in truth.
You also learned it from Epaphras our dear fellowservant. Epaphras is for you a faithful minister (servant) of Christ.
Epaphras also declared (told) to us your love in the Spirit.

For this cause we do not cease (stop) to pray for you. We have prayed since the day we heard it. We desire that you might be filled with the knowledge of His will. We pray you will have all wisdom and spiritual understanding.
We pray that you might walk worthy of the Lord, pleasing Him in everything. We pray you will be fruitful in every good work. We pray you will be increasing in the knowledge of God.
We pray you will be strengthened with all might, according to His glorious power. Then you will have all patience (enduring) and longsuffering (patience) with joyfulness.
Give thanks to the Father. The Father has made us meet (fit) to be partakers (sharers) of the inheritance. It is the inheritance of the saints (holy people) in light.
The Father has delivered (rescued) us from the power of darkness. He has translated (moved) us into the kingdom of His dear Son.
In the Son we have redemption (being bought back and set free) through His blood. We have the forgiveness of sins.
The Son is the image of the invisible (unseen) God. He is the firstborn of every creature.

For by Him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth. All things visible (seen) and invisible (unseen) were created by Him. This includes thrones, or dominions (lordships), or principalities (rulers), or powers. All things were created by Him, and for Him.
And the Son is before all things. By Him all things consist (hold together).
And the Son is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead. This is so that in all things He might have the preeminence (first place).
For it pleased the Father that in the Son should all fulness dwell (live).

Peace was made through the blood of the Son's cross. By the Son it pleased the Father to reconcile (bring back to God) all things to Himself. I say, by the Son, whether they are things in earth, or things in heaven.
And you were sometimes (once) alienated (cut off). You were enemies in your mind by wicked works. Yet now the Son has reconciled (brought back to God) you,
In the body of His flesh (human body) through death. This is to present you holy and unblameable (without blame) and unreproveable (with nothing against you) in His sight.

This is so if you continue in the faith, grounded (built) and settled. It is so if you are not moved away from the hope of the gospel (good news). You have heard that gospel (good news). It was preached to every creature which is under heaven. I Paul am made a minister (servant) of it.
I now rejoice in my sufferings for you. I fill up in my flesh (body) that which is behind (still lacking) of the afflictions (troubles) of Christ. I do this for His body's sake, which is the church.
I am made a minister (servant) of the church. This is according to the dispensation (work) of God which is given to me for you. It is to fulfil the word of God,
Even the mystery (secret) which has been hid from ages and from generations. But now it is made manifest (plain to see) to His saints (holy people).
To them God would make known the riches of the glory of this mystery (secret). It is among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). The mystery (secret) is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
We preach Christ, warning everyone, and teaching everyone in all wisdom. We want to present everyone perfect (complete) in Christ Jesus.
For this I also labour (work hard), striving according to His working. His working works in me mightily.

verses.text: For I would that you knew what great conflict (struggle) I have for you. I have it for those at Laodicea too. I have it for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh (in person).

I want their hearts to be comforted, being knit together in love. I want them to have all riches of the full assurance (being sure) of understanding. Then they may acknowledge (know) the mystery (secret) of God, and of the Father, and of Christ.
In Christ are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
And this I say so that no one should beguile (trick) you with enticing (smooth) words.
I am absent in the flesh (body). Yet I am with you in the spirit. I am joying and beholding (seeing) your order. I see the stedfastness (firmness) of your faith in Christ.
As you have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him.
Be rooted and built up in Christ. Be stablished (made firm) in the faith, as you have been taught. Abound (overflow) in it with thanksgiving.

Beware that no one spoils (robs) you through philosophy (human wisdom) and vain deceit (empty lies). Such things are after the tradition of men, after the rudiments (basic rules) of the world. They are not after Christ.
For in Christ dwells (lives) all the fulness of the Godhead (that He is God) bodily.
And you are complete in Christ. Christ is the head of all principality (rulers) and power.
In Christ also you are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands. You put off the body of the sins of the flesh (sinful self) by the circumcision of Christ.
You were buried with Christ in baptism. In baptism also you are risen with Christ through the faith of the operation (working) of God. God has raised Christ from the dead.
And you were dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh (sinful self). God has quickened (made alive) you together with Christ. God has forgiven you all trespasses (wrongs).
God blotted (wiped) out the handwriting of ordinances (written rules) that was against us. It was contrary (opposed) to us. God took it out of the way, nailing it to Christ's cross.
And having spoiled (stripped) principalities (rulers) and powers, God made a shew (show) of them openly. God triumphed over them in the cross.
So let no one judge you in meat (food), or in drink. Let no one judge you in respect of a holyday (feast day). Let no one judge you about the new moon, or the sabbath days (days of rest).
These are a shadow of things to come. But the body (the real thing) is of Christ.

Let no one beguile (cheat) you of your reward in a voluntary humility (false humility) and worshipping of angels. Such a person intrudes into those things which they have not seen. They are vainly (for nothing) puffed up by their fleshly (human) mind.
They do not hold the Head. From the Head all the body by joints and bands (ligaments) has nourishment ministered (supplied). The body is knit together, and increases with the increase of God.
So if you are dead with Christ from the rudiments (basic rules) of the world: Why, as though living in the world, are you subject to ordinances (rules) like these:
Touch not. Taste not. Handle not.
All these are to perish with the using. They are after the commandments and doctrines (teachings) of men.

These things indeed have a shew (show) of wisdom. They have will worship (self-made worship), and humility, and neglecting of the body. But they have no honour (value) against the satisfying of the flesh (sinful self).

verses.text: If you then are risen with Christ, seek those things which are above. Christ sits there on the right hand of God.
Set your affection (mind) on things above, not on things on the earth.
For you are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God.
Christ is our life. When Christ appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.

Mortify (put to death) therefore your members which are upon the earth. Put to death fornication (sexual sin), uncleanness (impure living), inordinate affection (wrong passion), evil concupiscence (evil desire), and covetousness (wanting what belongs to others). Covetousness (wanting what belongs to others) is idolatry (worshipping idols).
Because of these things the wrath (anger) of God comes on the children of disobedience (people who disobey God).
You also walked in these things some time (once), when you lived in them.
But now you also put off all these: anger, wrath (rage), malice (hate), blasphemy (insulting speech), and filthy communication (dirty talk) out of your mouth.
Do not lie one to another. You have put off the old man (old self) with his deeds.
And you have put on the new man (new self). The new man (new self) is renewed (made new) in knowledge after the image of God, who created it.
Here there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision. There is neither Barbarian (foreigner), Scythian (wild tribesman), bond (slave) nor free. But Christ is all, and in all.
Put on therefore, as the elect (chosen people) of God, holy and beloved (dearly loved): bowels (deep love) of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness (gentleness), longsuffering (patience).
Forbear (put up with) one another, and forgive one another. If anyone has a quarrel against any, forgive. Even as Christ forgave you, so also do you.
And above all these things put on charity (love). Charity (love) is the bond of perfectness (perfect unity).
And let the peace of God rule in your hearts. You are also called to peace in one body. And be thankful.
Let the word of Christ dwell (live) in you richly in all wisdom. Teach and admonish (warn) one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs. Sing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
Whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus. Give thanks to God and the Father by Him.
Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, as it is fit (right) in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives, and do not be bitter against them.
Children, obey your parents in all things. For this is well pleasing to the Lord.
Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, or they will be discouraged.

Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh (here on earth). Do not obey with eyeservice (working only when watched), as menpleasers (people pleasers). Obey in singleness (honesty) of heart, fearing God.
And whatever you do, do it heartily (with all your heart), as to the Lord, and not to people.
Know that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance. For you serve the Lord Christ.
But whoever does wrong will receive for the wrong which they have done. And there is no respect of persons (favoring anyone).

verses.text: Masters, give to your servants that which is just (right) and equal (fair). Know that you also have a Master in heaven.
Continue in prayer, and watch (stay alert) in it with thanksgiving.
At the same time, pray also for us. Pray that God would open to us a door of utterance (speaking). Then we may speak the mystery (secret) of Christ. For it I am also in bonds (chains).
Pray that I may make it manifest (plain to see), as I ought to speak.
Walk in wisdom toward those who are without (outside the church). Redeem (buy back) the time.
Let your speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt. Then you may know how you ought to answer everyone.
Tychicus will declare (tell) to you all my state. Tychicus is a beloved (dearly loved) brother, and a faithful minister (servant), and fellowservant in the Lord.
I have sent Tychicus to you for the same purpose. I want him to know your estate (how you are), and comfort your hearts.
Onesimus comes with Tychicus. Onesimus is a faithful and beloved (dearly loved) brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you all things which are done here.
Aristarchus my fellowprisoner salutes (greets) you. So does Mark, the son of Barnabas's sister. You received commandments about Mark: If he comes to you, receive him.
And Jesus, who is called Justus, greets you. These are of the circumcision (the circumcised Jews). These only are my fellowworkers to the kingdom of God. They have been a comfort to me.

Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, salutes (greets) you. Epaphras is always labouring (working hard) fervently (earnestly) for you in prayers. He prays that you may stand perfect (full-grown) and complete in all the will of God.
For I bear him record (tell you truly) that Epaphras has a great zeal (eagerness) for you. He has it for those in Laodicea, and those in Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved (dearly loved) physician (doctor), and Demas, greet you.
Salute (greet) the brothers who are in Laodicea. Salute (greet) Nymphas, and the church which is in his house.
And this epistle (letter) will be read among you. Then cause it to be read also in the church of the Laodiceans. And see that you also read the epistle (letter) from Laodicea.
And say to Archippus: Take heed (be careful) to the ministry (serving) which you have received in the Lord. Fulfil it.
I Paul write this salutation (greeting) with my own hand. Remember my bonds (chains). Grace be with you. Amen.
